items.title: Jerry Hey interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 2, 2023
items.q: Phil Collins, who played first in Cleveland — I mean Cincinnati for a long time, a really great player

ctx.x: Did the idea of becoming a trumpet player as a profession take a while to gel for you?

Yes it did. I started very early, because as I said my older brother was a trombone player and in the Boy Scouts he played the bugle for whatever, the Taps and Reveille and all that stuff in the Boy Scouts, and brought it home one day and literally I just picked it up when I was kind of two and then at age three I got my first trumpet and played with my mom in church on Mother’s Day. She played piano and I played then cornet. And so I started early and it was just something I always did. I didn’t really know…

This would have happened to you but I had this fascination with big bands when I was about that age and I remember my parents taking me to see what would have been the Glenn Miller ghost orchestra if you want to use that term, and I played the saxophone and I was staring up at them saying, “That’s what I really want to do.” Did you have that kind of experience?
